add_debug_tag.description: If true, adds DT_DEBUG tag to the .dynamic section.

add_needed_libs.description: List of dynamic library names to add as DT_NEEDED dependencies.

add_rpaths.description: List of RUNPATH directories to add to the existing RPATH/RUNPATH. Uses items schema for individual strings if nested, but here it is a simple list of strings for Jinja2 iteration compatibility with the constraint of flat items. To adhere strictly to 'items as a FLAT map', we interpret add_rpaths as a list of objects where the object has a single field 'path'.

add_rpaths_items.description: Internal schema descriptor for items of add_rpaths. Since Jinja2 lists of strings are harder to distinguish from other lists in this specific schema constraint without a name, we define the structure of the list elements. However, the prompt asks for `items` as a FLAT map. For a list of strings, this is tricky. Let's assume the user wants to add specific rpaths. If we must use a list of objects to satisfy the 'items map' requirement, we define the structure. But usually, rpaths are just strings. Let's look at `replace_needed_libs` which is clearly objects. For `add_rpaths`, standard patchelf usage is `--add-rpath /path`. A list of strings is most natural. If the schema requires `items` to be a map for lists, I will define `add_rpaths` as a list of objects with a single key `rpath` to be safe and consistent with the 'items as flat map' rule, although it's slightly verbose. Alternatively, I can leave `add_rpaths` as a list of strings if the 'items' constraint only applies to list-of-objects. The prompt says: 'For a list-of-objects, add `items` as a FLAT map'. So if it's a list of strings, I don't need items. I will use list of strings for simplicity unless it's clearly objects.

allowed_rpath_prefixes.description: List of prefixes to keep when shrinking RPATH.

clear_execstack.description: If true, clears the executable flag of the GNU_STACK program header.

force_rpath.description: If true, forces the use of the obsolete DT_RPATH instead of DT_RUNPATH.

input_file.description: The path to the ELF executable or library to be modified.

no_default_lib.description: If true, ignores default library search paths for dependencies.

output_file.description: The output file path. If empty, the input file is modified in place.

page_size.description: Uses the given page size instead of the default. 0 means default.

remove_needed_libs.description: List of dynamic library names to remove from DT_NEEDED dependencies.

remove_rpath.description: If true, removes the DT_RPATH or DT_RUNPATH entry.

rename_dynamic_symbols.description: Path to a file containing symbol rename mappings (old_name new_name).

replace_needed_libs.description: List of objects representing library replacements.

set_execstack.description: If true, sets the executable flag of the GNU_STACK program header.

set_interpreter.description: The path to the dynamic loader (ELF interpreter) to set.

set_os_abi.description: The OS ABI to set (e.g., 'Linux', 'System V').

set_rpath.description: The RUNPATH to set, replacing any existing RPATH/RUNPATH.

set_soname.description: The SONAME to set for the shared library.

shrink_rpath.description: If true, removes unused entries from RPATH/RUNPATH.
